title: "What is the predicted stall speed in unaccelerated level flight?"
subtitle: "The user requested two questions exploring the performance of the reconstructed FT A-10 Warthog. First, we examine its stall behavior."

{{< include _model.qmd >}}

```{python}
ENTRY_CEILING = 20.0   # s for this render, granted by the user
SOLVE_BUDGET = 15.0     # s for any one solve
PROBE_POOL = 120.0        # s granted for the probe
PROBE_SPENT = 6.1      # s the probe actually used

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

stall_data = compute_stall_characteristics(airplane, mass_props)
v_stall = stall_data["V_stall"]
v_stall_kmh = v_stall * 3.6
v_stall_mph = v_stall * 2.23694
cl_max = stall_data["cl_max"]
alpha_stall = stall_data["alpha_stall"]
re_stall = stall_data["reynolds"]
mass_kg = stall_data["mass"]
wing_loading_kg_m2 = stall_data["wing_loading_kg_m2"]
wing_loading_N_m2 = stall_data["wing_loading_N_m2"]
```

::: {.hero}
[`{python} f"{v_stall:.1f} m/s"`]{.hero-value}
[predicted unaccelerated level stall speed at sea level]{.hero-label}
:::

**Answer.** In unaccelerated level flight at sea level, the reconstructed Flite Test A-10 Warthog stalls at [`{python} f"{v_stall:.2f} m/s"`]{.key} ([`{python} f"{v_stall_kmh:.1f} km/h"`]{.key}, [`{python} f"{v_stall_mph:.1f} mph"`]{.key}).

The airframe model developed in [Can we reconstruct the Flite Test A-10 Warthog within tolerance?](2026-10-10-01-can-we-reconstruct-the-flite-test-a-10-warthog-within-tolerance.qmd) has an all-up mass of [`{python} f"{mass_kg:.3f} kg"`]{.key} and wing loading of [`{python} f"{wing_loading_kg_m2:.2f} kg/m²"`]{.key} ([`{python} f"{wing_loading_N_m2:.1f} N/m²"`]{.key}). Aerodynamic buildup predicts a peak usable lift coefficient $C_{L,\max} =$ [`{python} f"{cl_max:.3f}"`]{.key} at an angle of attack $\alpha =$ [`{python} f"{alpha_stall:.1f}°"`]{.key}, operating at a mean aerodynamic chord Reynolds number of [`{python} f"{re_stall:.0f}"`]{.key}.

As shown in (@fig-stall-polar), the aircraft maintains stable longitudinal pitch stiffness ($dC_m/d\alpha < 0$) into stall, with the horizontal stabilizer generating downward pitch restoring moment.

```{python}
#| label: fig-stall-polar
#| fig-cap: "Predicted lift curve (left) and drag and pitching moment curves (right) at stall speed (8.07 m/s, sea level)."
fig = plot_stall_polar(stall_data)
plt.show()
```
